comment: One row for each rule of the reference interpreter fir.interpreter
(src/fort/fir/interpreter.ft) and of its two entries in the driver, the mode --fir-run
and the pass `run` of --fir-test (src/fort/driver.ft). A row names the line that decides
the rule and a text that breaks it. The first stage runs the suite over FIR text
(test/fort/fir/interpreter_test.ft), the second the suite over fort source
(test/fort/fir/interpreter_source_test.ft), the third the driver suites, and the fourth
the run corpus against its native checked build (test/fir_run_test.py). The table runs
in the Linux VM with the debug preset and the default runner. The md5 guard reads the
product compiler, whose driver imports fir.interpreter. The first round of a run can
read stale (notes/testing.md 7), so the first row is one that a full run caught.

stages.name: the interpreter suite over FIR text
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 fir/interpreter_test

stages.name: the interpreter suite over fort source
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 fir/interpreter_source_test

stages.name: the driver suites
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 driver_run_test driver_abort_status driver_trap_status

stages.name: the run corpus
stages.command: python3 test/fir_run_test.py --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --cc clang --target x86_64-linux-gnu -j 4

mutations.old: return cast(v << cast(shift, u64), i64) >> shift;
mutations.new: return cast(v << cast(shift, u64), i64) >> shift & cast(ALL_BITS >> 1, i64);
mutations.what: a negative value of a narrow type reads as positive
a value loses its top bit at each width below 64

mutations.old: return (y > 0 && x > high - y) || (y < 0 && x < low - y);
mutations.what: a signed `+` below the minimum does not overflow

mutations.old: return (y < 0 && x > high + y) || (y > 0 && x < low + y);
mutations.what: a signed `-` above the maximum does not overflow
a negative product one past the minimum does not overflow

mutations.old: return a != 0 && b > wrap(ALL_BITS, w) / a;
mutations.new: return a != 0 && b > wrap(ALL_BITS, w) / a + 1;
mutations.what: an unsigned product one step past the maximum does not overflow

mutations.new:
if (y == -1 && x == low && w == 0) {
        fault(it, "division overflow");
mutations.what: the minimum divided by -1 has a result
a signed division drops the sign of its quotient

mutations.old: return wrap(cast(widen(a, w) >> cast(n, i64), u64), w);
mutations.what: `shr` of a signed value is logical
a count at the width shifts
a signed comparison compares the bits as unsigned

mutations.new:
case fir.rvalue_kind.rv_ne:
            return x < y || x > y;
mutations.what: `ne` of a NaN is false

mutations.new:
case fir.rvalue_kind.rv_fadd:
            return f32_bits(cast(cast(x, f64) + cast(y, f64) + 1e-9, f32));
mutations.what: an f32 sum is not rounded in f32
a float to i8 does not saturate at the i8 range
a signed integer reaches f32 through f64, rounded twice

mutations.old:
if (gen.gen_is_signed(from)) {
        return wrap(cast(widen(v, width(from)), u64), width(to));
mutations.new:
if (gen.gen_is_signed(from) && false) {
        return wrap(cast(widen(v, width(from)), u64), width(to));
mutations.what: a signed integer widens with zeros
each field of a struct starts at the start of the struct, not at its offset in the layout
a store writes its bytes big-endian
a positional aggregate writes the padding and a designated one does not zero it

mutations.new:
// a moved value passes its owner and its derivation, and no other tag
        it->sh.value = shadow.tag{shadow.origin{}, shadow.origin{}, it->sh.value.d};
mutations.what: a scalar `move` leaves its place as it was
`del` leaves its place as it was
`check(user)` fails on a true condition

mutations.old:
// a `check(overwrite: p)` continues (spec/ownership-design.md 3.2)
        go(it, k, t->target);
mutations.what: `check(overwrite: p)` ends the run

mutations.old:
values[n + 1] = cast(t->loc.line, u64);
    values[n + 2] = cast(t->loc.col, u64);
mutations.new:
values[n + 1] = cast(t->loc.col, u64);
    values[n + 2] = cast(t->loc.line, u64);
mutations.what: a failed check reports its column as its line
a `switch` never takes its first arm
the address of the last region that ended goes to the next region
a constant and the bytes of a string constant are writable
the compaction of the regions keeps the entries that ended and drops the live ones
a captured write to descriptor 2 lands in the stdout of the report
a captured descriptor is a terminal
a `calloc` whose size overflows multiplies anyway
`free` of an address inside an allocation releases it

mutations.old:
if (dst > src) {
        for (u64 mut k = n; k > 0; k--) {
mutations.new:
if (dst > src && false) {
        for (u64 mut k = n; k > 0; k--) {
mutations.what: a copy to a higher address that overlaps its source copies forward
`memcmp` gives the opposite sign
`snprintf` runs a format other than the one of std.rt and refuses the one of std.rt
`strtod` with an end pointer runs and writes no end
the errno accessor of Darwin is outside
`oracle_call` passes its function as the first argument
`exit(-1)` reports -1 and not the process status 255
the status of `main` is not masked to a byte
a frame that ends at the limit of the stack does not fit
a frame counts 8 bytes against the limit
the limit counts the locals of the new frame, so a run ends that native completes
a frame that ended still counts against the limit
the scalar result of a call is lost
a result wider than its place writes past the place
a designated initializer puts a member in the other field
an entry of an enum table holds the next value
an f32 constant keeps the binary64 pattern
`alloc` reports the column of its statement as its line

mutations.old:
u64 ptr = load(it, addr, WORD);
    shadow.derivation[1] mut from = {};
mutations.new:
u64 ptr = load(it, addr + WORD, WORD);
    shadow.derivation[1] mut from = {};
mutations.what: `del` frees the word after the pointer of its place
each bound of `slice_ptr` is sign-extended, so the `u8` 200 reads as -56
each bound of `slice_ptr` is zero-extended, so the `i8` -1 reads as 255
a `bool` load keeps its whole byte, so the byte 2 reads as `true`

mutations.old: put(it, at, size, load_value(it, src, t));
mutations.new: put(it, at, size, load(it, src, size));
mutations.what: a `bool` member or argument keeps the whole byte of its operand
the frame of the callee exists before its arguments are read, so a fault names the callee
an argument of `oracle_call` past the parameters is not read
the end of one region is the base of the next

mutations.old:
if (error != 0) {
        store(it, it->errno_slot, I32_SIZE, cast(error, u64));
mutations.new:
if (false) {
        store(it, it->errno_slot, I32_SIZE, cast(error, u64));
mutations.what: a range error of `strtod` leaves the errno of the run

mutations.old:
if (error != 0) {
        store(it, it->errno_slot, I32_SIZE, cast(error, u64));
mutations.new:
if (true) {
        store(it, it->errno_slot, I32_SIZE, cast(error, u64));
mutations.what: a call of `strtod` that sets no errno clears the errno of the run
the report of an aggregate result gives its first word
a slice starts `lo` bytes into its place
a `string` constant counts its NUL
a load through null is an invalid access
a store into read-only storage writes
a function that the lowering refuses ends the run as outside
a trap of an x86-64 run ends by SIGTRAP
`--` goes to the program as its first argument
a run that ends by a signal loses the buffered output of the compiler
--fir-run reads the interface of a used library
--fir-run --no-bounds-check runs the checked mode in silence
the pass `run` takes a signed value below the minimum of its parameter
the pass `run` takes an unsigned value past the maximum of its parameter
a test with the pass `run` writes the module after the reports
